I thought the performance would be poor but now I'm not so sure. 

I tested it with this:
```
import polars as pl
import time 

s = pl.Series("A", [x for x in range(100000)], dtype = pl.Int32)

start = time.time()
out = s.rolling_apply(window_size=3, function=lambda s: s.std())
print("rolling apply std")
print(time.time() - start)

start = time.time()
out = s.rolling_apply(window_size=3,
        function=lambda s: s.std(),
        weights = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
        )
print("rolling apply weights")
print(time.time() - start)
```

For the first piece, I get ~4.7s on the master branch and this branch. 
The second piece only runs on this branch and is slightly less than 4.7s.

Do you think the inefficiencies are getting optimised away or is this not a good example?

issue_context.title: Add missing arguments to rolling other functions
issue_context.body:
Right now, (as far as I can tell) all the rolling transforms have `weights`, `min_periods`, and `center` as arguments, except for the following:
- `rolling_median`
- `rolling_quantile`
- `rolling_skew`
- `rolling_apply`

It would be great if those arguments also get included there.
comments: @marcvanheerden I woudl ignore `rolling_skey` for now. It uses dynamic dispatch at the moment and is really slow and would be even slower with those args.
options added to rolling_median and rolling_quantile in https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/2229, will work on rolling_apply now in a separate PR
